L1 oracle: luaparse 0.3.1 (MIT), a Lua parser library independent of tree-sitter, run as calibration/oracles/luaparse/luaparse_dump.js (luaVersion LuaJIT, Node as a bench instrument only): every definition with a range, 4,265 on 662 files, 0 parse errors. Tier B on the D2 precedent (JavaParser, Roslyn, PSI, php-parser): an independent syntactic parser, so L1 can be excellent and L2 at most good. The tier is a claim for Opus review, not a harness fact. The parser is independent; the scope (a definition is a function stored in a statically named slot) is the dialect author's rule, written in the oracle's README, so sym_recall 1 and sym_precision 1 show the queries implement that rule over 4,265 real definitions, not that no other rule is reasonable.

L2 oracle: the grammar's own queries/tags.scm (tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-lua v0.5.0, MIT) run by py-tree-sitter 0.25.2 with tree-sitter-lua 0.5.0, tier C (D5, calibration/oracles/ts-tags), so L2 is capped at good. Its call pairs and the dialect's differ in attribution: upstream marks the whole table_constructor as the definition of its function-valued fields (a call written in a sibling field of a callback table such as pickers.new(opts, { prompt_title = .., attach_mappings = function .. end }) is paired with the first function field, 40 pairs on telescope's attach_mappings alone), and it has no definition for a string-keyed function or a t["k"] = function; the dialect pairs a call with the innermost function around it. Since the module symbol (K18) a call no function encloses is paired with the file's `<module>` symbol, and the oracle run pairs it the same way (tags_oracle.py --module-caller '<module>'): call_recall .9834 (15,079 of 15,334 pairs), call_precision .9701 (15,079 of 15,543).

L3 (LB-Q-lua, wave lang1): imports.scm reads `require` with a literal module name (`require("a.b")`, `require "a.b"`, `require 'a.b'`, `require [[a.b]]`) and `pcall(require, "a.b")`; the manifest's file-symbol strategy reads the dots as directory separators and tries a/b.lua then a/b/init.lua under the repository root, lua/, lib/ and src/ (package.path as Lua, OpenResty and Neovim projects lay it out). The dialect mints a LuaModule symbol per file (module_symbol, K18) so a require at the top of a file is an edge from that file's `<module>` to the required file's. Oracle: calibration/oracles/lua-require (tier B): luaparse for the statements and Lua 5.4.7's own package.searchpath for the lookup over the same package.path, so the strategy and the oracle share a path list (the operator's choice, stated) and nothing else. Tier B caps L3 at good. A require of a rock, a C module or a runtime-provided one (Kong 1,196 and telescope 49 of the literal names) names no file of the subject and is outside both. file_edge_recall 1 is against statements, not references (LB-F57): a file required and never used is in the truth.

file_edge_precision and file_edge_recall measured against an import dump's (file, imported file) pairs, there being no SCIP index: the truth is what each file's import statements name, not the files its references reach as a SCIP index's cross-file edges are, so a file reached without an import of its own (a file another one required, an autoloaded constant) is outside the truth and a resolved edge to it counts against precision, while a file imported and never referenced is in it (LB-F57)

universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B) is an unscored cross-check, not the L1 oracle: it writes no end line for Lua (range_agreement unmeasurable, L1 capped at good) and reads by pattern, not by parse. Over the same 662 files it reads sym_recall .9197, sym_precision .9826, kind_agreement 1, signature_coverage 1 (4,191 of 4,557 definitions matched; the incumbent walker read .2625 on telescope.nvim in the wave-0 baseline, docs/bench/readings/lang/baseline/lua.json). Its 366 unmatched definitions: 228 are text tagged as a function (a variable assigned the result of a call whose argument is a function, `local ok, err = pcall(function() ... end)`; an immediately invoked function expression; a string or table value on a line containing the word function; `type(v) ~= "function"` tagged as `~`), 122 are bracketed slots ctags spells by their key expression (`decoder[TAG.INTEGER] = function` is `INTEGER]`, `["k"] = function` is `["k"]`), and 16 sit inside block comments.
